body:
Same cause, second surface: the notification inbox.

Measured on the same local build (console in English through Preferences → Language, browser language zh-CN):

1. A sales manager approves one opportunity approval and rejects another.
2. The submitter opens the bell → **Notifications**. The UI is English, but the two decision notifications read 「请求已批准」 / 「请求已驳回」 with Chinese bodies, next to English rows.

The inbox list is fetched with `GET /api/v1/data/sys_inbox_message?top=20&sort=-created_at&filter=…` and, like the approvals fetch, carries no `Accept-Language`. Replaying that request by hand:

| `Accept-Language` | `title` of the two newest rows |
|---|---|
| `en` | `Request approved` / `Request rejected` |
| `zh-CN` | `请求已批准` / `请求已驳回` |

So the server resolves `keyed_text` correctly per request; the console just never tells it the UI language. Whatever fixes the approvals fetch should cover the `sys_inbox_message` (and `sys_notification_receipt`) reads too.

os-dev-report · #37483 · draft PR #37543 · head 3312d68bbf · CI green (38 success, 18 skipped by path, 0 failed)

**Outcome: no source change needed on `main`; the PR adds pins only.** The card was measured on the 18.6.0 bundles. On `main` the shared helper the card suggests already does it: `createAuthenticatedFetch` (`@object-ui/auth`) stamps `<html lang>` as `Accept-Language` on every `/api/` call, and every reader named here goes through it.

A1 census (on `main` 1af67b26):
- `useRecordApprovals` `fetchJson` (request, actions, remind) and `sharedUserFeeds` `fetchPendingApprovalPage`: bare `fetch` + `bearerAuthHeaders()` until #37185 (merged 2026-11-25, after 18.6.0), now `createAuthenticatedFetch`.
- `approvalsApi.ts`: `createAuthenticatedFetch` since #27040. `approvalRequestsDataSource.ts`: default `fetch` is `createAuthenticatedFetch` (#28619).
- Notification inbox (`sys_inbox_message`, `sys_notification_receipt`): read through the console adapter, which `AdapterProvider` builds on `withSettleSignal(createAuthenticatedFetch())`.
- `useRowApprovalLocks` (grid): lock booleans only, no server-rendered text; not in scope.

A2: the shared place is the helper itself; nothing to edit. A3 pins:
- `approvalsUiLocale-37483.test.tsx` (app-shell): approval history, remind, pending-approvals page, and a `sys_inbox_message` read through an adapter built as `AdapterProvider` builds it.
- `approvalRequestsDataSource.uiLocale-37483.test.tsx` (console): request page history and request read.
Each asserts `Accept-Language: en` under `<html lang="en">`, with a control (no UI language → no header). Ablation: replacing the stamp with a no-op turns the 6 positive pins red, the 3 controls stay green.

Open point: comment 7186322473 reports the inbox read without `Accept-Language`; the adapter has stamped it since October, and the unit pin does not reproduce that. If it still shows on a `main` build, it needs a browser capture of the actual request headers.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbGtuQD4c5iyX7mqpV

Inbox header capture on a `main` build (S2 of the REWORK on PR #37543).

**Result: the header is present.** With the console set to English on a zh-CN browser, `GET /api/v1/data/sys_inbox_message` carries `Accept-Language: en`. I could not reproduce comment 7186322473 on `main`.

Setup:
- Server: `examples/app-showcase`, `objectstack dev --seed-admin`, packages built from branch `claude/project-thread-17i5by`. The branch is `main` 1af67b26 plus two test files only.
- Console: `ui/apps/console` vite dev pointed at that server, so the current `ui/` source is what runs.
- Browser: Playwright Chromium with context `locale: 'zh-CN'` (`navigator.language` = `zh-CN`, browser default `Accept-Language` zh-CN). Console language English via `objectui-locale = en`, the key Preferences → Language writes. Signed in as the seeded admin.
- Headers read with `request.allHeaders()`, which gives what went on the wire.

| Run | `<html lang>` | `navigator.language` | Request | `Accept-Language` sent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UI English | `en` | `zh-CN` | `GET /api/v1/data/sys_inbox_message?top=20&sort=-created_at&filter=…` | `en` |
| UI English | `en` | `zh-CN` | `GET /api/v1/data/sys_notification_receipt?top=20&sort=-created_at&filter=…` | `en` |
| UI English | `en` | `zh-CN` | `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests?status=pending&approverId=…&limit=5` | `en` |
| Control: no UI language stored | `zh-CN` | `zh-CN` | the same three reads | `zh-CN` on each |

Reading: the inbox read already followed the UI language before #37185, and still does. So the card's inbox evidence is not explained by any change between 18.6.0 and `main`. Possible causes are a build that is not 18.6.0's source, or a UI language that was not actually `en` at read time. Nothing on `main` is missing the header, so I see no new finding.

The PR adds no source change because main already sends the UI language. It pins the approval reads and the inbox read through the real wiring, and those pins fail when the stamp is removed.

Evidence that the header is present on main is capture 7192984653. On a local main build (Playwright Chromium, browser locale zh-CN, UI language en), `GET /api/v1/data/sys_inbox_message`, `sys_notification_receipt` and `approvals/requests` all carried `Accept-Language: en`. In the control run, with no UI language stored, all three sent zh-CN.

Closing as completed. If a release build still shows a request in the browser's language instead of the UI language, reopen this card with a header capture from that build. Comment 7186322473's report on the inbox read could not be reproduced on main.
